title: INT 33h, the mouse driver services
covers: INT 33h, the mouse driver services selected by AX.

rows.text: Reset driver and read status, a call of the MS MOUSE driver.
The driver is reset.
AX is FFFFh when the hardware and driver are installed.
AX is 0000h when the hardware or driver is not installed.
BX is the number of buttons: 0000h other than two, 0002h two (many drivers), 0003h a Mouse Systems/Logitech three-button mouse, FFFFh two buttons.
Since INT 33 might be uninitialized on old machines, the caller should first check that it is neither 0000h:0000h nor points at an IRET (byte CFh).
To use the mouse on a Hercules-compatible monographics card in graphics mode, set 0040h:0049h to 6 for page 0 or 5 for page 1, then call this function.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x00 of its switch on AX, which jumps to the reset code under the label of case 0x21.
Stores false in the polled flag of the driver state.
With Mouse_Drv false the block is skipped: nothing is reset and AX keeps the 0000h it held on entry to case 0x00.
Show mouse cursor, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The mouse cursor is shown.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x01 of its switch on AX.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse the hide counter is set to 0.
Stores -1 in updateRegion_y[1], which the code comments as offscreen.
Hide mouse cursor, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The mouse cursor is hidden.
Multiple calls to hide the cursor require multiple calls to function 01h to unhide it.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x02 of its switch on AX.
Stores the time of the call in hidden_at when the hide counter was zero.
When the host's system cursor is in use and the mouse is not captured, the host pointer is hidden too.
Return position and button status, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
BX is the button status: bit 0 is 1 when the left button is pressed, bit 1 the right button, bit 2 the middle button (Mouse Systems/Logitech/Genius).
CX is the column.
DX is the row.
In text modes all coordinates are specified as multiples of the cell size, typically 8x8 pixels.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x03 of its switch on AX.
BL is the button state, which Mouse_ButtonPressed sets and Mouse_ButtonReleased clears per button; BH is GetWheel8bit, the CuteMouse wheel extension, so BX is more than the button state.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse BX is FFFFh if the right button is pressed, else 0, instead of BL and BH.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse AX is FFFFh if the left button is pressed, else 0.
Stores true in the polled flag and false in first_range_setx and first_range_sety.
With en_int33_hide_if_polling set, stores the time of the call in int33_last_poll.
Mouse_Reset sets the button state to 0.
Position mouse cursor, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The mouse cursor is positioned.
CX is the column.
DX is the row.
The row and column are truncated to the next lower multiple of the cell size, typically 8x8 in text modes.
Some versions of the Microsoft documentation incorrectly state that the coordinates are rounded.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x04 of its switch on AX.
The column and row are clamped to the minimum and maximum set by the range calls, and a value equal to POS_X or POS_Y is left unchanged.
With en_int33_hide_if_polling set, stores the time of the call in int33_last_poll.
Inside the range, CX and DX are stored as given when they differ from the current POS_X or POS_Y; these lines hold no truncation to the cell size.
Return button press data, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
BX is the button number: 0000h left, 0001h right, 0002h middle (Mouse Systems/Logitech/Genius mouse).
AX holds the button states.
BX is the number of times the specified button has been pressed since the last call.
CX is the column at which the specified button was last pressed.
DX is the row at which the specified button was last pressed.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x05 of its switch on AX.
A button number at or above MOUSE_BUTTONS is reduced to MOUSE_BUTTONS minus 1, and 0xFFFF selects the wheel data of the CuteMouse extension instead of a button.
BX is the button's press count, cleared on reading; with BX=0xFFFF the 16-bit wheel count from GetWheel16bit instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
AX is the button state, set by Mouse_ButtonPressed and cleared by Mouse_ButtonReleased, unchanged with BX=0xFFFF; with the PC-98 NEC mouse FFFFh if the left button is pressed, else 0.
CX is the button's last press column; with BX=0xFFFF the last scroll column instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
DX is the button's last press row; with BX=0xFFFF the last scroll row instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
Stores true in the polled flag.
With en_int33_hide_if_polling set, stores the time of the call in int33_last_poll.
Mouse_WheelMoved stores POS_X and POS_Y in last_scrolled_x and last_scrolled_y.
Mouse_Reset sets the button state, last_scrolled_x and last_scrolled_y to 0.
Return button release data, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
BX is the button number.
AX holds the button states.
BX is the number of times the specified button has been released since the last call.
CX is the column at which the specified button was last released.
DX is the row at which the specified button was last released.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x06 of its switch on AX.
A button number at or above MOUSE_BUTTONS is reduced to MOUSE_BUTTONS minus 1, and 0xFFFF selects the wheel data of the CuteMouse extension instead of a button.
BX is the button's release count, cleared on reading; with BX=0xFFFF the 16-bit wheel count, cleared instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
AX is the button state, set by Mouse_ButtonPressed and cleared by Mouse_ButtonReleased, unchanged with BX=0xFFFF; with the PC-98 NEC mouse FFFFh if the left button is pressed, else 0.
CX is the button's last release column; with BX=0xFFFF the last scroll column instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
DX is the button's last release row; with BX=0xFFFF the last scroll row instead; with the PC-98 NEC mouse always the left button's.
Stores true in the polled flag.
With en_int33_hide_if_polling set, stores the time of the call in int33_last_poll.
Mouse_WheelMoved adds the scroll to the wheel counter, limited to -0x7FFF to 0x7FFF; GetWheel8bit and GetWheel16bit clear it and Mouse_Reset sets it to 0.
Mouse_WheelMoved stores POS_X and POS_Y in last_scrolled_x and last_scrolled_y.
Mouse_Reset sets the button state, last_scrolled_x and last_scrolled_y to 0.
Define horizontal cursor range, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The horizontal range the cursor can move in is defined.
CX is the minimum column.
DX is the maximum column.
In text modes the minimum and maximum columns are truncated to the next lower multiple of the cell size, typically 8x8 pixels.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x07 of its switch on AX.
The minimum and maximum are stored directly from the int16 values of CX and DX, the smaller as minimum.
The cursor x is clamped into the new range.
With assume_max_x 0, and first_range_setx set or no button down, a range from 0 sets the screen maximum x, rounded to the mode width when near it.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse the range is stored from CX and DX; with it no range is set.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse the call returns the right button press data in AX, CX, DX and BX and clears its count.
The button state that the PC-98 NEC mouse call returns in AX is set by Mouse_ButtonPressed, cleared by Mouse_ButtonReleased and set to 0 by Mouse_Reset.
Define vertical cursor range, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The vertical range the cursor can move in is defined.
CX is the minimum row.
DX is the maximum row.
In text modes the minimum and maximum rows are truncated to the next lower multiple of the cell size, typically 8x8 pixels.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x08 of its switch on AX.
The minimum and maximum are stored directly from the int16 values of CX and DX, the smaller as minimum.
The cursor y is clamped into the new range.
With assume_max_y 0, and first_range_sety set or no button down, a range from 0 sets the screen maximum y, rounded to the mode height when near it.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse the range is stored from CX and DX; with it no range is set.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse the call returns the right button release data in AX, CX, DX and BX and clears its count.
The button state that the PC-98 NEC mouse call returns in AX is set by Mouse_ButtonPressed, cleared by Mouse_ButtonReleased and set to 0 by Mouse_Reset.
Define graphics cursor, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 3.0 and later.
The graphics cursor is defined.
BX is the column of the cursor hot spot in the bitmap (-16 to 16).
CX is the row of the cursor hot spot (-16 to 16).
ES:DX points to the mask bitmap.
In graphics modes the screen contents around the cursor position are ANDed with the screen mask and then XORed with the cursor mask.
The Microsoft mouse driver v7.04 and v8.20 uses only BL and CL, so the hot spot row and column should be limited to -128..127.
A Microsoft KnowledgeBase article states that the high bit is right-most, which all other available documentation contradicts.
The bitmap is 16 words of screen mask followed by 16 words of cursor mask; each word is one row of sixteen pixels, low bit rightmost.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x09 of its switch on AX.
Stores 2 in the cursor type.
Without the NEC mouse CURSORY times 2 bytes each of screen and cursor mask are read from ES:DX; with it CURSORY times 2 big-endian words go to the cursor mask.
Define text cursor, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 3.0 and later.
The text cursor is defined.
BX selects the cursor: 0000h software, 0001h hardware.
With the software cursor CX is the screen mask.
With the software cursor DX is the cursor mask.
With the hardware cursor CX is the start scan line.
With the hardware cursor DX is the end scan line.
With the software cursor the character and attribute data at the screen position are ANDed with the screen mask and then XORed with the cursor mask.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x0a of its switch on AX.
Any nonzero BX, not only 0001h, selects the hardware cursor: the cursor type is stored as 1, otherwise 0.
textAndMask and textXorMask are stored from CX and DX whatever BX holds, the hardware cursor included.
Read motion counters, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
CX is the number of mickeys the mouse moved horizontally since the last call.
DX is the number of mickeys the mouse moved vertically.
A mickey is the smallest increment the mouse can sense.
Positive values indicate down and right.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x0b of its switch on AX.
CX is the horizontal counter, to which Mouse_CursorMoved adds whole mickeys, only while the host mouse is captured, else 0; the counter is cleared in either case.
DX is the vertical counter, to which Mouse_CursorMoved adds whole mickeys, only while the host mouse is captured, else 0; the counter is cleared in either case.
Stores true in the polled flag.
Mouse_CursorMoved subtracts 65536 from a mickey counter at 32768 or more and adds it at -32769 or less.
Mouse_Reset sets both mickey counters to 0.
Define interrupt subroutine parameters, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The interrupt subroutine parameters are defined.
CX is the call mask: bit 0 mouse moves, bits 1-2 left press and release, bits 3-4 right, bits 5-6 middle (Mouse Systems/Logitech/Genius); bits 7-15 unused.
ES:DX points to the FAR routine to call.
Some versions of the Microsoft documentation incorrectly state that CX bit 0 means call if the mouse cursor moves.
The routine is called with AX the condition mask, BX the button state, CX and DX the cursor column and row, SI and DI the horizontal and vertical mickey counts.
Some versions of the Microsoft documentation erroneously swap the meanings of SI and DI.
In text modes the row and column are reported as a multiple of the character cell size, typically 8x8 pixels.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x0c of its switch on AX.
Light pen emulation on, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
Light pen emulation is turned on.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
Only logs an error that light pen emulation on is not implemented; nothing else is done in the call.
Light pen emulation off, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
Light pen emulation is turned off.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
Only logs an error that light pen emulation off is not implemented; nothing else is done in the call.
Define mickey/pixel ratio, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The mickey to pixel ratio is defined.
CX is the number of mickeys per 8 pixels horizontally.
DX is the number of mickeys per 8 pixels vertically.
The default is 8 mickeys per 8 pixels horizontally and 16 vertically.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x0f of its switch on AX.
Nothing is stored unless both CX and DX, taken as int16, are nonzero.
Define screen region for updating, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 1.0 and later.
The screen region for updating is defined.
CX and DX are the X and Y coordinates of the upper left corner of the region.
SI and DI are the X and Y coordinates of the lower right corner of the region.
The mouse cursor is hidden in the specified region.
The cursor needs to be explicitly turned on again.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x10 of its switch on AX.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse no update region is set and the horizontal cursor range is stored instead; otherwise the region is stored.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse CX and DX, the smaller first, are stored as the horizontal cursor range; otherwise as the region's upper left corner.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse SI and DI are not read; otherwise they are stored as the region's lower right corner.
Get number of buttons, a call of Genius Mouse 9.06.
AX is FFFFh.
BX is the number of buttons.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x11 of its switch on AX.
AX is 0x574D, an identifier for detection purposes, not FFFFh.
BX is 0, reserved capability flags, not a button count; CX is set to 1 to say the wheel is supported.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse CX and DX, the smaller first, are stored as the vertical cursor range instead.
Set large graphics cursor block, a call of the MS MOUSE driver.
The large graphics cursor block is set.
BH is the cursor width in words and BL the horizontal hot spot (-16 to 16).
CH is the number of rows in the cursor and CL the vertical hot spot (-16 to 16).
ES:DX points to the bit map of the screen and cursor maps.
AX is FFFFh if the call is successful.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x12 of its switch on AX.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse the call only logs an error that it is not implemented: BX is not read and no cursor is set.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse BX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse CX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse ES:DX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
Without the PC-98 NEC mouse AX is not set to FFFFh: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse the drawn cursor background is restored.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse BX is stored whole as the drawing plane, not read as BH width and BL hot spot.
Define double-speed threshold, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 5.0 and later.
The double-speed threshold is defined.
DX is the threshold speed in mickeys per second.
A DX of 0000h means the default of 64 per second.
The stored threshold is the speed above which the cursor's on-screen motion is doubled.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x13 of its switch on AX.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse no threshold is stored; otherwise DX is stored as the threshold, 64 if DX is 0.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse DX is not read; otherwise it is stored as the threshold speed.
With the PC-98 NEC mouse BX is set to FFFFh, to enable plane 3.
Exchange interrupt subroutines, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 3.0 and later.
The interrupt subroutine is exchanged for the one given.
CX is the call mask of the new routine.
ES:DX points to the new FAR routine.
CX is the call mask of the previous interrupt routine.
ES:DX is the FAR address of the previous interrupt routine.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x14 of its switch on AX.
Return driver storage requirements, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
BX is the size of the buffer needed to store the driver state.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x15 of its switch on AX.
Save driver state, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The driver state is saved in the buffer.
BX is the size of the buffer.
ES:DX points to the buffer for the driver state.
Although not documented, many drivers appear to require BX on input, since the Microsoft driver does not use it.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x16 of its switch on AX.
The bytes of the driver structure, sizeof(mouse) of them, are copied to ES:DX.
BX is not read: sizeof(mouse) bytes are always written, whatever BX holds.
Restore driver state, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The driver state is restored from the buffer.
BX is the size of the buffer.
ES:DX points to the buffer holding the saved state.
Although not documented, many drivers appear to require BX on input, since the Microsoft driver does not use it.
Some mouse drivers range-check the saved values against the current video mode, so the video mode should be restored first.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x17 of its switch on AX.
The bytes at ES:DX, sizeof(mouse) of them, are copied over the driver structure.
BX is not read: sizeof(mouse) bytes are always copied, whatever BX holds.
Set alternate mouse user handler, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
An alternate user handler is set for the call mask.
CX is the call mask: bit 0 moves, bits 1-4 left and right presses and releases, bits 5-7 shift, ctrl, alt during the event; one of 5-7 must be set.
ES:DX points to the FAR routine invoked on mouse events.
AX is 0018h if successful and FFFFh on error.
Up to three handlers can be set by separate calls, each with a different combination of shift states in the call mask.
A call with a call mask of 0000h undefines the specified handler (official documentation); the same mask with address 0000h:0000h does too (real life).
Some versions of the documentation erroneously reverse the order of the bits in the call mask.
The handler is called with AX the condition mask, BX the button state, CX and DX the cursor column and row, SI and DI the mickey counts; registers are preserved.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x18 of its switch on AX.
No alternate handler is set: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
CX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
ES:DX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
AX is not stored: it keeps the 0018h it held on entry, the success value, while the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
No handler is defined: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
No handler is undefined: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
Return user alternate interrupt vector, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The user event handler defined by function 18h whose call mask matches CX is looked for.
CX is the call mask (as for function 18h).
BX:DX is the user interrupt vector.
CX is the call mask, 0000h if not found.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x19 of its switch on AX.
No handler is looked for: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
CX is not read: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
BX and DX are not set: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
CX is not set: the call only logs an error that it is not implemented.
Set mouse sensitivity, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The mouse sensitivity is set.
BX is the horizontal speed (see function 0Fh).
CX is the vertical speed (see function 0Fh).
DX is the double speed threshold (see function 13h).
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1a of its switch on AX.
BX is clamped to 100, stored in senv_x_val and turned into the factor senv_x, (BX-1) squared over 3600 plus a third.
CX is clamped to 100, stored in senv_y_val and turned into the factor senv_y, (CX-1) squared over 3600 plus a third.
DX is clamped to 100 and stored in dspeed_val.
The factors senv_x and senv_y are computed only when both BX and CX are nonzero.
Return mouse sensitivity, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
BX is the horizontal speed.
CX is the vertical speed.
DX is the double speed threshold.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1b of its switch on AX.
Mouse_SetSensitivity limits each of its three values to 100 and stores them in senv_x_val, senv_y_val and dspeed_val.
Set interrupt rate, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The mouse interrupt rate is set.
BX is the interrupt rate: 00h no interrupts allowed, 01h 30 per second, 02h 50 per second, 03h 100 per second, 04h 200 per second.
The call is only available on an InPort mouse, and values greater than 4 may cause unpredictable driver behavior.
Nothing is returned: the list gives this call no Return line.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1c of its switch on AX.
No interrupt rate is set: the case body holds only a comment that the rate cannot really be set because it is host determined, and a break.
BX is not read: the case body holds only a comment that the rate is host determined, and a break.
Define display page number, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The display page number is defined.
BX is the display page number.
The stored display page number is the page on which the cursor will be displayed.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1d of its switch on AX.
Only BL, the low byte of BX, is stored in mouse.page; the high byte BH is not used.
Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode stores 0 in mouse.page.
Return display page number, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
BX is the display page number.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1e of its switch on AX.
Disable mouse driver, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
AX is the status: 001Fh successful, FFFFh unsuccessful.
On success ES:BX is the INT 33 vector from before the mouse driver was first installed.
The call restores the vectors for INT 10 and INT 71 on an 8086, or INT 74 on a 286 or 386.
If INT 33 is restored to ES:BX, the driver will be completely disabled.
Many drivers return AX=001Fh even though the driver has been disabled.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x1f of its switch on AX.
AX is not stored in this case: no line of it sets the status.
BX and ES are both set to 0, and a comment says the old driver vector is zero at the moment, a TODO.
No vector is restored: the case stores false in mouse.enabled, saves mouse.hidden in mouse.oldhidden, and sets mouse.hidden to 1.
If the cursor was not hidden, the case also stores the PIC time index in mouse.hidden_at.
Enable mouse driver, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
AX is the status: 0020h successful, FFFFh unsuccessful.
The call restores the vectors for INT 10h and INT 71h on an 8086, or INT 74h on a 286 or 386, which function 1Fh removed.
Microsoft's documentation states that no value is returned.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x20 of its switch on AX.
AX is not stored in this case: no line of it sets the status.
No vector is restored: the case stores true in mouse.enabled and copies mouse.oldhidden to mouse.hidden.
Software reset, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
AX is FFFFh if the mouse driver is installed.
AX is 0021h if the mouse driver is not installed.
BX is the number of buttons, FFFFh meaning two buttons.
The call is identical to function 00h, but does not reset the mouse.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x21 of its switch on AX.
With Mouse_Drv false the block is skipped: the case stores neither AX nor BX.
Mouse_Reset sets the mickey to pixel ratio through Mouse_SetMickeyPixelRate with 8 and 16, which stores the four conversion factors.
Mouse_Reset zeroes the mickey counters and accumulators, the button state, the wheel counter and the last scroll position.
Mouse_Reset zeroes the press and release counts and positions of every button.
Mouse_Reset sets mouse.x and mouse.y to half of mouse.max_x + 1 and mouse.max_y + 1, mouse.sub_mask to 0 and mouse.in_UIR to false.
BX is set to MOUSE_BUTTONS, which is defined as 3.
Set language for messages, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
The language for messages is set.
BX is the language: 00h English, 01h French, 02h Dutch, 03h German, 04h Swedish, 05h Finnish, 06h Spanish, 07h Portugese, 08h Italian.
The call is only available on international versions of the driver; US versions ignore it.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x22 of its switch on AX.
The case tests no driver version: it stores BX in mouse.language on any driver.
Get language for messages, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.0 and later.
BX is the language, coded as in the set language call (table #03177).
The US version of the driver always returns zero.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x23 of its switch on AX.
BX is copied from mouse.language, which the set language case stores from BX, or which Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode sets to 0.
Get software version, mouse type and IRQ number, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.26 and later.
BX is 0000h to check for the function's existence.
AX is FFFFh on error.
BH is the major version.
BL is the minor version.
CH is the type: 1 bus, 2 serial, 3 InPort, 4 PS/2, 5 HP.
CL is the interrupt: 0 for PS/2, 2 for IRQ2, 3 for IRQ3, on to 7 for IRQ7, on to 0Fh for IRQ15.
The function appears to have been present as early as version 6.02 although Microsoft documents version 6.26; for earlier versions use INT 33/AX=006Dh.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x24 of its switch on AX.
BX is not read: the case stores BX, CH and CL and has no use of the value BX held on entry.
AX is not stored in this case: the error value FFFFh is not set.
Get general driver information, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.26 and later.
AX is the general information, whose bits are described by table #03178.
Bit 15 of AX is set if the driver was loaded as a device driver rather than a TSR.
Bit 14 of AX is set if the driver is the newer integrated type.
Bits 13 and 12 of AX are the current cursor type: 00 software text cursor, 01 hardware text cursor, 1X graphics cursor.
Bits 11 to 8 of AX are the interrupt rate, coded as in the set interrupt rate call (table #03176).
Bits 7 to 0 of AX are the count of currently-active Mouse Display Drivers (MDD), the newer integrated driver type.
BX is the cursor lock flag, for OS/2, to prevent reentrancy problems.
CX is the mouse code active flag, for OS/2.
DX is the mouse driver busy flag, for OS/2.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x25 of its switch on AX.
AH is built from 0x40, the cursor type shifted left by 4 and 0x01: no constant sets bit 7 of AH, the device driver bit.
The interrupt rate bits are the constant 0x01, commented as 30 reports per second.
AL is set to the constant 1, commented as a guess for the number of display drivers.
BX is set to 0.
CX is set to 0.
DX is set to 0.
Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode stores 0 in mouse.cursorType.
Get maximum virtual coordinates, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 6.26 and later.
BX is the mouse-disabled flag: 0000h mouse enabled, nonzero disabled.
CX is the maximum virtual X for the current video mode.
DX is the maximum virtual Y.
For driver versions before 7.05 the call returns the currently-set maximum coordinates; version 7.05 and later returns the absolute maximum coordinates.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x26 of its switch on AX.
CX and DX are copied from mouse.max_x and mouse.max_y, with no choice by driver version.
Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode stores true in mouse.enabled.
Mouse_AfterNewVideoMode sets the maxima, mouse.max_x to 639 and mouse.max_y to 479, unless setmode is true with a video mode above 0x13.
Get screen and cursor masks and mickey counts, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 7.01 and later.
AX is the screen-mask value.
BX is the cursor-mask value.
For version 7.02 and later, AX is instead the hardware cursor scan-line start.
For version 7.02 and later, BX is instead the hardware cursor scan-line stop.
CX is the horizontal mickeys moved since the last call.

Load acceleration profiles, a call of the MS MOUSE driver version 7.0 and later.

The profile data starts with four BYTE lengths, one for each of profiles 1 to 4, at offsets 00h to 03h.
At offsets 04h, 24h, 44h and 64h come 32 BYTEs of threshold speeds for profiles 1 to 4.
At 84h, A4h, C4h and E4h come 32 BYTEs of speedup factors for profiles 1 to 4, where 10h is 1.0, 14h 1.25, 20h 2.0 and so on.
At 104h, 114h, 124h and 134h come the 16 BYTE blank-padded names of profiles 1 to 4.
Unused bytes in the threshold speed fields are filled with 7Fh and unused bytes in the speedup factor fields with 10h.

Get version string, a call of the MS MOUSE driver.
ES:DI points to the Microsoft version number of the resident driver.
The version number is two BYTEs: the major version at offset 00h and the minor version, in BCD, at offset 01h.
There seems to be no reliable method to distinguish MS MOUSE before 3.00 from mouse drivers of other vendors.
Some releases of MS MOUSE 6.00 erroneously return 6.01 instead of their true version; a DI value of 01ABh can then still detect a 6.00 driver.
For returned versions 6.02 and later, INT 33/AX=0024h should be used to retrieve more accurate version data.
True MS MOUSE drivers can be identified by a magic number stored one byte after the copyright string, found by scanning the first 2 Kb of the driver's segment.
The magic numbers are 5564h for versions 3.00 to 6.00, 557Ch for 6.01Z to 6.24, E806h for 6.25, EB02h for 6.26 to 7.04, 0800h for integrated 1.0+.
Versions above 7.04, except integrated drivers, have a magic number representing their version, e.g. 0507h for version 7.05.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by the case 0x6d of its switch on AX.
ES:DI is not set: the call only logs an error that get version string is not implemented.
INT 33h AX=53C1h gets the static device data and the driver support status.
The function returns the device type and version number of the connected SWIFT device, and informs the application whether the installed mouse driver supports SWIFT calls.
ES:DX is the address of the Static Device Data buffer.
AX is the return status: 1 means the driver supports SWIFT functions, any other value means not; the capture reads the 1 as a lower-case L.
ES:DX is the buffer address, the same as the input.
Byte 0 of the static device data is the device type, byte 1 the major version number and byte 2 the minor version number.
Bytes 3 to 8 hold the X, Y, Z, pitch, roll and yaw coordinate descriptors; the capture's glyphs are garbled in these lines.
Byte 9 of the static device data is reserved.
Device type 0 means no SWIFT device connected, 1 a Logitech CyberMan, and 2 to 255 are reserved for Logitech SWIFT devices.
The device major version number is, for example, 1 for version 1.50, and the minor is 50 for version 1.50 or 3 for version 1.03.
In a coordinate descriptor, bits 0-3 are the bits of resolution (0..15) and bit 5 is return to center, with 1 meaning return to center.
In a coordinate descriptor, bit 6 is absolute when 1 and relative when 0.
Bits 4 and 7 of a coordinate descriptor are reserved.
Bits of resolution is the number of bits the device uses to encode the coordinate, and the positions it generates may be somewhat fewer.
The CyberMan uses 2 bits of resolution for Z, pitch, roll and yaw, but generates only 3 distinct values for them.
Return to center means the device returns to the neutral, absolute 0 position when the user releases it or stops applying force.
The INT 33h handler reaches it by case 0x53C1 of its switch on AX.
